messages:
jane.support: Customer (ellen.customer) reporting recurring 504s from Hosted API when sending large prompt + attachments (context.jsonl). Started ~2025-06-03 09:12 UTC. Customer says requests time out after ~12s. curl they used below.

ellen.customer: Confirmed — happens every time we include the 18MB context file. Works if we strip down to <1MB.

jane.support: Trace IDs from customer: trace=abc123def, trace=def456ghi. Edge response: 504 Gateway Timeout. Example response headers: 
  HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Time-out
  Server: envoy
  x-request-id: abc123def
  via: 1.1 redwood-edge

matt.eng-sre: Can you paste the exact curl? Also we need the edge logs (cluster/health) around those trace ids. Any recent infra changes?

jane.support: curl repro they ran:
  curl -v -X POST https://api.redwoodai.com/v1/generate \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    --data-binary '@payload-with-context.jsonl' --http2

jane.support: Pasted relevant edge excerpt (sanitized):
  [2025-06-03T09:12:07Z] trace=abc123def upstream_rq_timeout
  [2025-06-03T09:12:07Z] cluster: model-pool-us-east-2 no healthy upstreams
  [2025-06-03T09:12:07Z] connection error: "TLS record size > MTU", fractured records?

lee.eng-runtime: "TLS record size > MTU" note stands out. Large bodies + HTTP/2 can surface record fragmentation on some NLBs. Is the customer hitting IPv6 or a path that could be MTU-limited? Also: any LB/NLB rolling change today?

tom.infra: We rolled an NLB agent update at 09:04 UTC (small config tweak to connection draining). TTLs are short for the internal model-pool service (10s). If DNS flaps + record fragmentation happen, envoy might mark upstream unhealthy briefly. I'll check NLB host metrics.

deploy-bot: infra: nlb-agent-stable rollout started by tom.infra at 2025-06-03T09:04:12Z

matt.eng-sre: Repro instructions for SRE: try reproduce locally with the same file size + http2: 
  curl -v --http2 --header 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @large-context.json 
  https://edge.redwoodai.internal/v1/generate -H 'x-debug-trace: sre-repro'
  Watch envoy logs for upstream health-check events and "connection timeout" / "no healthy upstreams" messages.

jane.support: I ran the repro from a staging host, got 504 after ~12s. Edge log trace id xyz789 shows upstream connect timeout and immediate 504 response.

ana.product: Customer impact? How many requests affected and SLA risk? Do we need to issue incident notification?

matt.eng-sre: Early count: 4 customers reported similar 504s in the 09:10-09:20 window, all with payloads >8MB. I think this is an edge-path + large payload pattern, not a single tenant.

lee.eng-runtime: Mitigations we can try ASAP:
  - increase edge upstream connect timeout from 10s -> 20s as stopgap
  - enable per-route upstream-buffering for large streaming requests (prevents fragmentation exposure)
  - add fallback routing to model-pool-us-east-2-large-mtu pool (hosts with tuned MTU/keepalive)
I'll prepare a canary and coordinate with infra to roll to a small subset.

tom.infra: I'll pause further agent rollouts and check NLB MTU/path MTU metrics. If we confirm fragmentation, we can flip to the large-mtu pool and revert the agent change.

jane.support: Ok will tell customer we're investigating and ask them to avoid attaching >8MB for now. I'll share repro curl and next steps.

ellen.customer: Thanks — please keep me posted. We can short-term upload the context to S3 and reference it instead of embedding if that helps.

matt.eng-sre: Next actions: 1) infra: confirm NLB change correlation (tom.infra) 2) runtime: prepare canary route + timeout bump (lee.eng-runtime) 3) support: communicate workaround to customer (jane.support). I'll open a P0 if counts increase.

jane.support: Acked. Will update when we have canary results. :thumbsup:
